reply_text:
@references alone leave most R-patterns isolated, so I'm checking which graph "giant connected component" refers to.Two useful finds: library patterns carry an `@holds-at R9` field, and the graph you mean is the mined pattern graph. Checking both:㊥ (a third route via the pattern graph) Yes. 52 library patterns already carry an R-number directly, in an `@holds-at` field; `aif/no-self-certification` has `@holds-at R9`, pegged to the R9 paragraph of `sec-catalog.tex`. 46 of those 52 are in the giant component of the mined pattern graph, so a third route works for most R-numbers. When the turn bids land, I'll add a graph-distance assignment to the same collation. Where the two routes agree on a pattern, we can take that pattern as aligned with more confidence.

㊢ (what the graph has) The graph is `storage/operator-turns/mined-pattern-graph.json`, built by `futon3c/scripts/mined_pattern_graph.py` and last generated on 30 September. Its giant component has 621 of 912 patterns. The edges come from operator-turn analyses: why, how, co-cited, rejected-beside and next-in-session. Each R-number usually has an `aif/…` pattern, a `problems/rN-…` pattern and sometimes a `war-room/…` one.

How the R-tagged patterns connect to the 100 patterns in the turn sample (65 of which are in the giant component):

| How connected | R-numbers |
|---|---|
| Well connected | R2, R5, R9, R10, R15, R20 (`aif/no-self-certification` has degree 18 and 34 sampled patterns within two steps) |
| Thinly connected | R3, R4, R6, R8, R11, R12, R13, R14, R16, R17 (0–8 sampled patterns within two steps) |
| Outside the giant component | R1, R7 (their R1/R7 patterns aren't in it), R3a and TRACE (no edges at all) |

🈖 (how the third route would work) For each sampled pattern, look at which R-tagged patterns are within one or two steps, and weight the nearer ones more. That gives each pattern a spread over R-numbers from graph position alone, with no agents involved. The graph records how patterns come up together in your turns, while the turn bids record what you do in a turn. So the two routes are fairly independent. One caution on edge types: next-in-session is the largest (1,712 edges) and the weakest, so I'd compute one version with all edges and one with only why, how and co-cited.

㊩ (gaps the graph can't cover) R1 and R7 sit outside the giant component, and R3a and TRACE have no edges, so for those four the turn bids will be the only evidence. The graph is also a day old. I'd regenerate it first; `mined_pattern_graph.py` is a registered command, so that's cheap.

previous_reply_acts.text:
(how it's set up) Everything is in `futon0/analysis/audits/rnode-turn-bids/`, committed as `7c1471f`.
- **Sample:** the top 100 patterns by hits, three turns each, chosen at random with a fixed seed. Each turn is shown with the end of the agent message it answered (145 of the 300 have one).
- **Blinding:** turns have opaque ids T001–T300 and no pattern, and agents are told not to look the records up. The key is kept in a separate `key.json`.
- **Priming:** each node starts from the claims its agent wrote about its code in the first round. That saves re-reading the code.
- **What counts as a bid:** a turn in which you yourself do what the node does. A turn that only talks about the node doesn't count.
- **Bid contents:** each bid quotes your exact words and says in one sentence what they take in or produce in the node's terms. At most 30 bids per node.
- **Checker:** confirms every quote appears word for word in its turn. I checked that it catches an invented quote and a made-up turn id.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text:
(R14 pilot) R14 (commitment temperature) made 11 bids, and they read right to me. Three examples:
- T027, "don't come back to me until it's done or there's a major issue": a firm commitment, with the one condition for reopening it.
- T238, "take that as written for now, and we can always adjust later": a commitment held loosely.
- T273, "j7 stay off (but come back to this later)…": four candidates, each given its own level of commitment.

previous_reply_acts.text: (a caution on the counts) Three turns per pattern is thin. A pattern's spread over R-nodes will be suggestive, not measured. The stage-level picture pools 300 turns, so it will be firmer. It shows whether the nodes' bids stay within each pattern's stage label.
